mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing consumer and business spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a low FEDFUNDS rate, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1800 units signals strong consumer demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic strength and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the 60-day windows when HOUST exceeds 1800, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE) and high payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows when UNRATE is below 4% and PAYEMS is above 150000, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production (INDPRO) during a late-cycle expansion signals potential supply chain constraints and reduced corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of the 60-day windows when INDPRO growth slows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% indicates a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Real consumer spending (RSAFS) growth indicates strong demand, which supports corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 5-day windows when RSAFS growth is positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows when UNRATE is below 3.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A divergence between industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP (GDPC1) growth rates indicates potential supply chain disruptions, which can negatively impact corporate earnings and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows when INDPRO and GDPC1 diverge, the hypothesis is rejected.
